title: Counit identity for the inverse-image/pullback comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix composable scheme isomorphisms $Z\xrightarrow{h}W\xrightarrow{k}V$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], completed coefficients and an object $N\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $C_{k,\bullet}$ be the strict quotient tower used in the definition of $Lk^*N$, and identify $M=Lk^*N$ with $R\lim C_{k,\bullet}$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-limit, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Let $h^*C_{k,\bullet}$ be the tower obtained by applying the finite pullback levelwise, and let $u_{h,C_k}:h^{-1}C_{k,\bullet}\to h^*C_{k,\bullet}$ be its termwise unit map, whose components send $x$ to $x\otimes1$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Write $\epsilon_{C_k}:\Delta R\lim C_{k,\bullet}\to C_{k,\bullet}$ and $\epsilon_{h^*C_k}:\Delta R\lim h^*C_{k,\bullet}\to h^*C_{k,\bullet}$ for the derived-limit counits on strict towers, each given by a K-injective tower resolution $q:C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] as $[q]^{-1}$ composed with the ordinary limit-cone map $\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet$, the normalization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. If $\eta_{h,k,N}:F_{h,E}F_{k,E}N\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim h^*C_{k,\bullet}$ is the comparison used in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and $\kappa^h_M:h^{-1}M\to F_{h,E}M$ is the specified inverse-image/pullback comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], then, under $M=R\lim C_{k,\bullet}$, $$\epsilon_{h^*C_k}\circ\Delta(\eta_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^h_M)=u_{h,C_k}\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon_{C_k})$$ as morphisms of strict quotient towers from $\Delta h^{-1}M$ to $h^*C_{k,\bullet}$. Thus the counit image of $\eta_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^h_M$ is the termwise map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ applied to the counit tower, before any realization or reduction.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: the counit identity for eta composed with the inverse-image/pullback unit

proof.text: Put $C=C_{k,\bullet}$, $D=h^*C$ and $H=h^{-1}$. All restrictions to the completed coefficient sheaf are implicit. Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P'\to M$ actually used to define $F_{h,E}M$ and $\kappa^h_M$, and put $B_m=P'\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}(A_{E,m})_W$ and $C_h=h^*B_\bullet$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Write $r:\Delta P'\to B_\bullet$ for the strict quotient map and $u_B:HB_\bullet\to h^*B_\bullet$ for the termwise finite unit. The compatible family defining the integral comparison is $\theta^\Delta=u_B\circ H(r):\Delta HP'\to C_h$, by part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Thus $F_{h,E}M=R\lim C_h$ and $\kappa^h_M$ is the class of the cone lift of this family followed by $[H(q)]^{-1}$. In particular its defining cone is built from $C_h$, not from $D$. The resolution $P'$ of $M$ is separate from the representative of $N$ that produced $C$.

source.place: Global powers, agent expansion: distinguish the two completed-pullback resolutions

proof.text: On either scheme the strict tower category is abelian and $\Delta$ is exact, since kernels and cokernels are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The ordinary bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(X,\lim T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta X,T)$ sends a map to its compatible projections. Apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to $G=\Delta$, $F=\lim$. Here $L\Delta=\Delta$ by exactness and $R\lim$ exists on the whole derived tower category and is computed by K-injective towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its characterizing formula, using the identity resolution on the $\Delta$ side, identifies the derived bijection with $e_T(a)=\epsilon_T\circ\Delta(a)$: on $T\to I$ it is precisely the ordinary limit cone transported through that resolution, as normalized in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Functoriality in the tower variable therefore gives, for every derived tower morphism $\psi:T\to T'$, $$\epsilon_{T'}\circ\Delta(R\lim\psi)=\psi\circ\epsilon_T.$$ This applies to a derived morphism represented by a roof, as well as to a strict chain map.

source.place: Tags 0FND and 0DVC, functoriality of derived adjunction; with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 for the K-injective tower computation

proof.text: Keep the whole quotient diagram. Set $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_\bullet=((A_{E,m})_W)_m$. Use the small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, so $\Delta R\to S_\bullet$ is a morphism of sheaves of rings on that site. Indeed $S_\bullet(m,U)=(A_{E,m})_W(U)$ is a sheaf because coverings are at fixed $m$. Its modules are quotient-coefficient diagrams; restriction $U$ to $\Delta R$-modules is exact since underlying sheaves, kernels and cokernels are unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Change of rings $L$ on this site is computed by K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The complex $\Delta P'$ is K-flat: for an acyclic diagram $A$, each $A_m$ is acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and $(A\otimes_{\Delta R}\Delta P')_m=A_m\otimes_R P'$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its terms are flat by the same levelwise test. Consequently $L(\Delta P')=B_\bullet$. The ordinary change-of-rings adjunction on this site is given by $f\mapsto(x\mapsto f(x\otimes1))$, with inverse $g\mapsto(x\otimes a\mapsto a g(x))$; these formulas respect restrictions and sheafification by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], hence give inverse maps of Hom sets. Apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with this exact restriction functor and the everywhere-defined $L$. Its fraction formula identifies the derived unit at $\Delta P'$ with the strict map $r$. Thus derived adjunction sends $\phi:B_\bullet\to C$ to $U(\phi)\circ r$, in the derived category of whole towers.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sheaf change-of-rings adjunction on the small tower site; derived.tex Tags 0FND/0DVC; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY

proof.text: Let $e'=\epsilon_C\circ\Delta[q]:\Delta P'\to UC$. Under the diagram adjunction of Step 3 let $\phi:B_\bullet\to C$ be its adjunct. Explicitly this is $L(e')$ followed by the quotient-module action, the counit of change of rings. These are exactly the arrow and normalization used in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]; K-flat computation is that of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Hence $$\eta_{h,k,N}=R\lim(h^*\phi):R\lim C_h\to R\lim D.$$ By the characterizing adjunct formula in Step 3 (equivalently the unit-counit identity), $$U(\phi)\circ r=e'=\epsilon_C\circ\Delta[q].$$ Both equalities concern derived morphisms of the entire quotient diagram. They do not assert that $\phi$ can be chosen as a levelwise map of the given representatives. Suppress $U$ henceforth when reading $\phi$ as a morphism of completed-coefficient towers.

source.place: Tag 06YY, derived change of rings; agent specialization of the normalized comparison construction to the counit of C

proof.text: Countable products of completed module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Therefore [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies the cone used in part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] with $R\lim C_h$, using precisely the cone map of a K-injective tower resolution followed by the inverse of the zero-shifted-component inclusion. Under this normalized identification the cone lift from Step 1 is $r_\theta:HP'\to R\lim C_h$ of [lem-trf-integral-cone-counit-realization]. That lemma, applied to $C_h$ and its strict compatible family $\theta$, gives $$\epsilon_{C_h}\circ\Delta(r_\theta)=\theta^\Delta=u_B\circ H(r),\qquad \kappa^h_M=r_\theta\circ[H(q)]^{-1}.$$ It is $r_\theta$, rather than $\eta\circ\kappa^h_M$, to which the cone-counit identity applies.

source.place: Tag 0941, K-injective limit/cone comparison; agent application of the normalized cone-counit identity to C_h

proof.text: The finite map $u_T:HT\to h^*T$ from part (a) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] is natural in a quotient-coefficient tower complex $T$: for any chain map $v$, both $h^*v\circ u_T$ and $u_{T'}\circ H(v)$ send a section $x$ to $v(x)\otimes1$. This equality survives sheafification and commutes with the quotient transitions, so it is an equality of strict tower chain maps. Both $H$ and the finite-level $h^*$ are exact [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and hence preserve quasi-isomorphisms of such diagrams, whose acyclicity is levelwise. For a roof $T\xleftarrow{s}T''\xrightarrow{v}T'$ the two strict naturality equalities for $s$ and $v$, after inverting $H(s)$ and $h^*(s)$, give the same square for the derived morphism $[v][s]^{-1}$. Apply this to $\phi$ from Step 4. Then in the derived tower category $$h^*(\phi)\circ\theta^\Delta=h^*(\phi)\circ u_B\circ H(r)=u_C\circ H(\phi\circ r)=u_C\circ H(\epsilon_C)\circ\Delta[H(q)].$$ Here $H$ commutes with $\Delta$ termwise, and the last equality is the whole-diagram adjunct identity of Step 4.

source.place: Tag 03D6, tensor-unit formula for module pullback; agent naturality calculation on complexes and roofs

proof.text: Apply Step 2 to the derived tower arrow $h^*\phi:C_h\to D$ and compose with $\Delta(r_\theta)$. Using Steps 4, 5 and 6 gives $$\begin{aligned}\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(\eta_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^h_M)\circ\Delta[H(q)]&=\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(R\lim(h^*\phi))\circ\Delta(r_\theta)\\&=h^*\phi\circ\epsilon_{C_h}\circ\Delta(r_\theta)\\&=h^*\phi\circ\theta^\Delta\\&=u_C\circ H(\epsilon_C)\circ\Delta[H(q)].\end{aligned}$$ Exactness of $H$ makes $H(q)$ a quasi-isomorphism; cancel its invertible class on the right. Since $D=h^*C$ and $u_C=u_{h,C_k}$ this proves the requested identity in the derived category of strict towers. The description $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ refers to the actual unit $u_C$ after $H(\epsilon_C)$; it does not describe a map on $H\lim I$ defining $\kappa$.
